text: Noel, a member says we told them Cedar Ridge closes at 21:00.
I told them 21:00. I read it off the card at the phone.
I have a printed card in my hand. It says 17:00.
The card on the phone says 21:00. That is the one I read to the member.
Then we are not holding the same card. Mine is printed. It says 17:00.
The one in the sleeve by the handset says 21:00. The member heard 21:00 because that is what I said.
The printed card is the card for that phone. It says 17:00.
It was not the card in the sleeve when I took the call.
I printed it for the sleeve. I am holding that sheet.
Read me the words on your sheet.
Cedar Ridge closes at 17:00. That is what the printed card says.
The sleeve card says: if the caller asks when Cedar Ridge closes, say 21:00.
Those are two cards. I am asking which one is on the phone.
The sleeve. It says 21:00. That is the card on the phone. I used it.
The printed card is the phone card. It says 17:00. Another sheet in the sleeve would be the wrong sheet.
Or the printed card never reached the phone, and the card on the phone is the one I read.
I do not agree. The card I printed is the one for the phone.
I do not agree with that. I was at the phone. I read 21:00. The member was told 21:00.
What you told them is 21:00. That still does not settle which card is on the phone.
What I said came off the card that was at the phone. That card says 21:00.
The printed card says 17:00, and that printed card is the one I count as the phone card.
Then we have already split. You have a card that says 17:00. The handset has a card that says 21:00.
Put them in one place before either of us calls the member again.
They are side by side now. Sleeve card says 21:00. Your printed card says 17:00.
Two cards on the desk does not pick which one is on the phone.
The card in the sleeve is the one I read. I am calling that the card on the phone.
The sleeve can hold a card that is not the printed phone card. I am not giving you the sleeve as the answer.
And I am not calling your printed card the one I read from. I read 21:00 at the phone.
You say the card on the phone says 21:00. I say the card on the phone is the printed one, and it says 17:00.
Yes. We do not agree which card is on the phone.
I will not tell the next member 21:00 from your sleeve while I am holding a printed card that says 17:00.
I will not tell the next member 17:00 from a card that was not at the phone when I read the close.
Then neither of us gives a close until we agree which card is on the phone. We do not agree.
We do not agree. The member was told 21:00. Your printed card says 17:00. The card I read at the phone says 21:00. That is where this sits.
